West Newton is the Newton land west of King George Boulevard and north of Highway 10.
Its City plans run generally south of 68 Avenue to Highway 10, in three areas: West Newton North, West Newton South and West Newton / Highway 10.
Scott Road (120 Street) is the west edge toward Delta, and the wider Newton community is bordered by Delta west, 160 Street east and Whalley and Fleetwood north.
The West Newton plans are largely residential, with park and institutional uses mixed in.
The schools named inside the plan areas are J.T. Brown Elementary, Panorama Park Elementary and Tamanawis Secondary, at 12600 66 Avenue.
South of the residential plans, the Highway 10 / Highway 99 side carries industrial and mixed-employment land, not housing.

blocks.text: West Newton: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000 allows one secondary suite per single-family, semi-detached or duplex unit, no suite inside a coach house or garden suite, and a suite floor area of at most 40% of the principal unit.

Small-scale multi-unit housing (SSMUH) in Surrey allows at most 3 units on lots under 280 square metres, 4 units on larger lots, and up to 6 units on eligible lots of at least 281 square metres within 400 metres of a frequent bus stop.

A coach house or garden suite is allowed in residential zones that allow detached houses, duplexes and houseplexes, sized 35 to 75 square metres, rising to 120 square metres on some larger zones, with one extra parking space.
A short-term rental in Surrey is an owner-hosted rental under 90 consecutive days, the owner must live there as a primary residence, and a business licence at $358 per year is required.
West Newton South was rescinded by the Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan (OCP) update, so that area is now led by the OCP, not the old plan.

blocks.text: West Newton: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Newton takes its name from Elias John Newton, whose homestead sat along 72 Avenue near 124 Street.
The Newton Cultural Commercial District strategy covers a commercial district at 128 Street and 80 Avenue in West Newton.
Newton Elementary opened in 1914 at what is now King George Boulevard and 72 Avenue, the corner that became Newton's main commercial district after King George Boulevard was completed in 1940.

blocks.text: West Newton: development and new projects

items.t: The City is creating a new Newton–King George Boulevard plan to guide growth along King George Boulevard, at the area's east edge.

A $5.3-million road contract awarded February 9, 2026 covers the 70 Avenue extension from King George Boulevard to 138 Street, supporting the future Newton Community Centre east of King George Boulevard.
Surrey's 2026 municipal total residential rate is $1.84251 per $1,000 of assessed value, before other authorities' rates.
The 2026 annual flat rate for a single-family home is water $1,195 plus sewer $1,661, total $2,856; a secondary suite adds $1,275.71.
Surrey property taxes are due July 2, with a 5% penalty after July 2 and a further 5% after September 2.
The City of Surrey is a designated taxable area for the provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax (SVT).
Newton Exchange is the local exchange, confirmed by TransLink as the terminus of both the R1 and the R6.
Highway 10 forms the south edge and Highway 99 employment land sits at the plan area's south, giving the area two highway edges.

blocks.text: West Newton: risks and due diligence

items.t: The south end drains toward the Serpentine and Nicomekl lowlands, the dyke-protected floodplain south of Newton; check a specific lot on the City's lowlands floodplain pages.
Do not rely on the rescinded West Newton South plan for permitted use; the City states the OCP now leads development there.

blocks.text: With RapidBus on both sides, West Newton is a family-house area: the R1 on King George Boulevard by Newton Exchange to the east, and the R6 on Scott Road to the west.

faq.a: The R1 RapidBus on King George Boulevard (Newton Exchange to Guildford Exchange), the R6 Scott Road RapidBus on the west edge (Scott Road Station to Newton Exchange), and routes 323 and 364 through the area — two RapidBus corridors connecting to Expo Line stations.

faq.q: Is West Newton in a floodplain or the ALR?
faq.a: The residential upland is outside the Serpentine & Nicomekl lowland floodplain, which lies to the south and is dyke-protected; the south end of the plan area falls toward those lowlands, and a specific property's flood and ALR status must be checked on the City's flood mapping and the Agricultural Land Commission's maps.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in West Newton?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 89 houses listed with 8 sold in the month and 107 condos and townhomes listed with 18 sold in the month in West Newton. Those are month-end counts and move daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is West Newton a buyers’ or sellers’ market?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses had a sales ratio of 9%, a buyers’ market; condos and townhomes had a sales ratio of 17%, a balanced market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.
